articles.title: Planktonic hyperiidean amphipod confirmed in the Aegean Sea, and a new study shows how to identify subadult males
articles.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
articles.summary: Amphipods change in size and shape each time they molt. When a species is told apart from its relatives by small anatomical details, this creates a practical problem: a trait that identifies an adult may be absent or different in the younger animal. A recently published study in Biodiversity Data Journal tests this problem on Phronima atlantica, a planktonic amphipod of the open ocean, and identifies which of its features stay reliable in males from the subadult to the adult stage.

articles.title: Earth's next ice age may have already begun. Global warming stopped it
articles.summary: Scientists have uncovered surprising evidence that Earth’s next ice age may have already begun, only to be stopped by global warming. By studying ancient plants preserved beneath the Barnes Ice Cap in the Canadian Arctic, researchers discovered that the remnants of a massive ice sheet began expanding again about 2,000 years ago, signaling the possible start of a new glacial period. But by the 1960s, rising temperatures had reversed that growth, causing the ice to shrink instead.
